newsitem.title: USA: U.S. counter-sues Iran over damages to U.S. ships.
newsitem.headline: U.S. counter-sues Iran over damages to U.S. ships.

text.p: The United States has sued Iran for damages to U.S. warships and U.S.-flagged vessels in the latest round of legal battles stemming from the Iran-Iraq war, the State Department's top lawyer said on Tuesday.

The U.S. claim against Iran, which did not specify the amount of damages sought, was filed with the International Court of Justice in the Hague on Monday in response to related Iranian claims against Washington, lawyer Michael Matheson said.

"We're claiming for damages done by Iranian forces in attacking U.S.-owned and U.S.-flagged vessels in the (Persian) Gulf during the Iran-Iraq war," Matheson, whose formal title is acting legal advisor, said in an interview with Reuters.

The court, the judicial arm of the United Nations, dealt the United States an initial setback last December in the case. It ruled it would hear an Iranian claim for damages related to the destruction of three Iranian oil platforms by U.S. warships 10 years ago.

The dispute stems from the final stages of the 1980-88 war between Iran and Iraq. At the time, the United States had reregistered Kuwaiti oil tankers under its flag to give them U.S. Navy protection from Iranian attack.

Matheson said the U.S. decision to file a counterclaim had "nothing to do with any political events in Iran." Instead, he said, it was tied to the conduct of the pending suit, which Iran brought in November 1992 and which officials said could drag on for years.
